questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

He had hardly gone a few kilometres ______ his car broke down.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **when**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 'Hardly' and 'when' are **correlative conjunctions**.
 
• **Correlative conjunctions** are sort of like tag-team conjunctions. They come in pairs, and you have to use both of them in different places in a sentence to make them work. They get their name from the fact that they work together (co-) and relate one sentence element to another.
 
 
• For example: **Hardly** had I reached the station **when** the train left.
 
 
 
• Similarly, in this question, the **conjunction** that must fit the blanks should be 'when' as 'hardly' is present in the former part of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: *He had hardly gone a few kilometres **when__** his car broke down.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__***

 
• Some of the important **Correlative Conjunctions** are:

 
 
• Either….or
 
• Neither….nor
 
• **Hardly….when**
 
• Scarcely….when
 
• Both…and
 
• If…then
 
• Not only….but also
 
• Rather….than
 
• Whether…or
 
• No sooner…than
 
• Else…but
 
• Lest…should
 
• Other…than
 
• So…that

questions.question:

The assignment __was so difficult__ for Mohit to do all by himself.
questions.solution:
__
 
• **The correct answer is option 1 i.e. 'was too difficult'.**
 
• **Rule**__: The adverb '**too**' should be followed by "**adjective + to infinitive(to + V1)**". 
 
 
• In the given sentence, the adjective (difficult) is followed by 'to + V1' i.e. 'to + do'.
 
• So, according to the rule, the adverb **'so' should be replaced by 'too'**.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct sentence is 'The assignment **was too difficult** for Mohit to do all by himself.'

questions.question:

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Rule**__: If** two actions take place in the past**, one after the other, the **first action** will be in the** Past Perfect **Tense and the **second action** will be in the **Simple Past** Tense.
 
• In the given sentence, the** first action** is in the **past perfect** tense. 
 
• The structure of the past perfect tense is** 'Subject + had + V3 + object'. **
 
• So, the **second action **should be in the **Simple Past **Tense i.e. **'subject + V2 + object'**.

 

Therefore, **option 2** 'reached' which is in **V₂ form** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

Plenty of information about the flora and fauna of India ______ available in this book
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3 i.e. is.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the **subject** is '**information**' which is an uncountable noun.

 
 
• Although an uncountable noun has a plural meaning, most uncountable nouns (like information, administration, management, advice, accommodation) are singular with no plural form.
 
• **Uncountable nouns** are always followed by the **singular verb**. This is in accordance with the Subject-Verb Agreement rule.
 
 
 
• So, **option 1 and 4** get eliminated.
 
• **Option 2** is also eliminated since **'has' **(as well as have) will always be followed by V3.
 
• Therefore, the suitable verb that fits in the given context is** 'is'.**
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 3.**

**Correct Sentence:__ ***Plenty of information about the flora and fauna of India __**is**__ available in this book*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment. If no substitution is required select 'No substitution'**

The student, along with his parents, __were asked for waiting __outside the Principal's office.
questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is option 1 i.e. was asked to wait**
 
• In the given sentence, the **verb 'was' should be used** in the place of 'were' as it is referring to the **singular subject 'the student'.**
 
 
• **Rule**: Expressions such as **'as well as, along with, together with, and others'** do not act as coordinating conjunctions.
 
• Therefore, when you use these expressions to join one singular subject of a sentence with another noun or pronoun, you do not form a plural subject. **The verb should appear in the singular.&
lt;/strong>
 
 
 
• Therefore, out of given alternatives, singular verb is used only in option 1 i.e. 'was asked to wait'.**
